Sunday, November 22

Game recap

EDM4CAR7Final: EDM 4, CAR 7

Edmonton led 3-1 in Raleigh, which in Oilers terms is the part of the horror movie where somebody says they'll be right back. Owen Michaels, Leon Draisaitl (his 22nd, on the power play) and a shorthanded Mathieu Joseph built the lead, and then Carolina scored six of the next seven. Jalen Chatfield, Taylor Hall and Andrei Svechnikov struck in a 3:05 stretch of the second, Sebastian Aho put the Hurricanes ahead for good on the power play with 26 seconds left in the period, and Svechnikov and Alexander Nikishin finished it. Carolina scored three power-play goals, and Aho had a goal and two assists. Pyotr Kochetkov won while stopping 11 of 15, a save percentage usually reserved for beer league. Devon Levi faced 36 shots and a penalty kill that kills nothing but Edmonton's evenings.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI4CGY3OTFinal: CHI 4, CGY 3 OT

Dillon Boucher and Adam Klapka dropped the gloves four seconds in, which turned out to be the most organized thing Calgary did all night. Ryan Strome gave the Flames the lead, then Chicago scored three times in 3:05 of the second: Roman Kantserov's 10th, Ryan Donato with the extra attacker on and Patrick Kane on the power play. Calgary clawed back through Jonathan Castagna and a Yegor Sharangovich power-play goal early in the third, but Sam Rinzel ended it at 4:45 of overtime, his third point of the night. Kane, who apparently plans to do this until the sun burns out, had a goal and two assists. Spencer Knight stopped 33 of 36; Dustin Wolf stopped 29 of 33 and deserved a better cause. The Flames got a point, which is what Calgary calls a moral victory and the standings call 3-on-3 charity.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3FLA4Final: BUF 3, FLA 4

Sam Bennett spent Saturday treating the Sabres like a rental car. He scored three minutes in, answered Jack Quinn's go-ahead goal 18 seconds later, and put Florida in front shorthanded 48 seconds into the third for the hat trick, his eighth, ninth and 10th of the season. Buffalo, to its credit, kept getting up: Jiri Kulich, Quinn and Tage Thompson (his 15th) each tied or led. So Bennett went and set up Sandis Vilmanis for the winner with 3:18 left, a four-point night. Jacob Markstrom needed only 16 saves on 19 shots. Alex Lyon stopped 26 of 30 and is 0-3-1 since coming back, and Lindy Ruff said his team got beat at the net front on the winner. The Sabres are 9-10-4, a record that looks exactly like every Sabres record you have ever seen.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT3NSH4Final: PIT 3, NSH 4

The Penguins led 2-0 in Nashville, and Andrei Kuzmenko, a healthy scratch in five of the previous six games, scored his first goal in black and gold. That was the good part, and it lasted about 70 seconds. Jonathan Marchessault got one back before the first period ended, Filip Forsberg and Reid Schaefer scored in the first 6:22 of the second, and after Hendrix Lapierre tied it at 3, Jayden Struble won it 3:31 into the third off feeds from Steven Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly. Marchessault and Brady Skjei had two points each, Juuse Saros stopped 21 of 24, and Sergei Murashov made 25 saves in the loss. Samuel Girard had the other Pittsburgh goal with Tommy Novak in the top-line seat beside Sidney Crosby. Ottawa's general manager watched from the press box, and the Penguins played like a team that knew the store was open.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH5BOS7Final: WSH 5, BOS 7

Elias Lindholm scored four goals, and at no point did anyone in a Capitals sweater seem interested in finding out where he was standing. He scored on the power play in the first, twice in the second and again 4:07 into the third, and set up David Pastrnak in between for a five-point night. Morgan Geekie had three assists, Tanner Jeannot scored, and even Jeremy Swayman picked up an assist while stopping 30 of 35. Washington kept it a game: Tom Wilson, a shorthanded Alex Tuch, Pierre-Luc Dubois and Dylan Strome had it tied 4-4 in the second, and Jakob Chychrun made it 6-5 late before Fraser Minten hit the empty net. Charlie Lindgren allowed six on 22 shots. That's five straight losses and a sub-.500 record for the Capitals, and Spencer Carbery said that if you cannot defend in this league, you will never win. Seven goals against is a strong supporting argument.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CBJ4TOR3Final: CBJ 4, TOR 3

The Maple Leafs led 3-1 at home and lost, because of course they did, and because the hockey gods have a sense of humor the winning rally ran through Matthew Knies, the winger Toronto traded to Columbus in September. Auston Matthews (his 14th, on the power play), Jake McCabe and Teddy Blueger built the lead. Knies set up Adam Fantilli's power-play goal in the second, tied it himself, unassisted, with 4:20 left, and 52 seconds later Zach Werenski scored the winner from Fantilli. Cam Talbot made 23 saves; Anthony Stolarz stopped 31 of 35 and has seen this movie. That's nine straight losses, 0-8-1, for an 8-14-3 team whose coach, Jim Hiller, called the night just not National Hockey League level. Toronto has spent decades finding new ways to lose. Getting beat by its own trade is at least efficient.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI4MTL3Final: PHI 4, MTL 3

Montreal spent the third period erasing a two-goal deficit and the last 31 seconds finding out none of it mattered. Noah Cates scored at 19:29, from Sean Couturier and Matvei Michkov, and the Flyers walked out of the Bell Centre with both points and most of the building's good mood. Christian Dvorak opened the scoring, Oliver Kapanen answered 16 seconds later, and Denver Barkey (a goal and an assist) and Rasmus Ristolainen made it 3-1 in the second, both set up by Owen Tippett. Zachary Bolduc on the power play and Owen Beck tied it 74 seconds apart early in the third. Dan Vladar stopped 20 of 23. Jacob Fowler saw 20 shots and four of them went in, which is a rough way to spend a Saturday night in front of 21,000 amateur goalie coaches. The Canadiens did the hard part and then forgot the easy part: the last half-minute.

Game recap

LAK2OTT4Final: LAK 2, OTT 4

For most of two periods the Kings led 1-0 on a Mats Zuccarello goal and played the kind of hockey that makes you check your phone. Then Nick Cousins tied it with 54 seconds left in the second, and Tim Stützle decided the third period was his. He scored 30 seconds in, set up Stephen Halliday's power-play goal at 5:54 and scored again at 7:16: three Ottawa goals in 6:46, three points for Stützle, his 12th and 13th of the season. Dylan Cozens and Jake Sanderson had two assists each. Linus Ullmark stopped 19 of 21 and was mostly asked to stay awake. Anton Forsberg made 24 saves, and Quinton Byfield's late goal made the score look friendlier than the period was. Los Angeles held a lead for two periods and had no idea what to do with it, the same way it handles the first round.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI3DET2Final: NYI 3, DET 2

Ondrej Palat came into the night with two goals all season and left Detroit with four, which tells you what kind of evening the Red Wings had. Emmitt Finnie put Detroit up in the first, Palat tied it in the second, Simon Holmstrom scored his 10th early in the third to stretch his point streak to seven games, and Palat's second made it 3-1. Alex DeBrincat answered 29 seconds later, and that was all. Matthew Schaefer had two assists and now has 85 career points, passing Rasmus Dahlin for the second most by a teenage defenseman; only Phil Housley had more. Ilya Sorokin stopped 18 of 20, John Gibson 18 of 21, and Ben Chiarot and Brayden Schenn fought late in the second for the purists. The Islanders have points in seven straight. Detroit managed 20 shots at home, a rebuild now old enough to ask for the car keys.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD6STL9Final: NJD 6, STL 9

Fifteen goals in St. Louis, and somewhere a goalie coach is updating his resume. The Blues led 3-0 before six minutes were gone on goals from Brandon Carlo, Jimmy Snuggerud (his 13th, on the power play) and Robert Thomas, and when Philip Broberg made it 4-1 at 9:03, Connor Hellebuyck's night was over: four goals on six shots. Jake Allen came in and gave up four more. Jake Neighbours had five assists, the kind of line you normally need a video game to produce, and Broberg, Thomas and Logan Mailloux each had a goal and two assists. New Jersey never went away, getting within one twice on goals from Timo Meier, Luke Hughes and Connor Brown, but Pavel Buchnevich, Mailloux, Mason McTavish and Jonatan Berggren (twice, one into the empty net) kept answering. Jordan Binnington allowed six on 43 shots and won comfortably. The Devils scored six and lost by three, which is less a hockey game than a cry for help.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK5WPG4SOFinal: VGK 5, WPG 4 SO

Adam Lowry scored 29 seconds in and the Jets still found a way to hand out a souvenir point and keep none of the good ones. Vegas answered through Brett Howden and Mitch Marner, Viggo Björck tied it before the first intermission, and the teams traded from there: Tomas Hertl's 10th on the power play, Mark Scheifele, then Kyle Connor's 19th to put Winnipeg up 4-3 early in the third. Ivan Barbashev tied it with 3:35 left, and in the shootout William Karlsson scored the only goal while Carter Hart turned away Scheifele, Connor and Gabriel Vilardi. Jack Eichel had two assists, Hertl and Howden a goal and an assist each. Hart stopped 26 of 30; Stuart Skinner made 29 saves and lost anyway. Winnipeg led twice at home and went 0-for-3 in the skills contest, proof that you can change the goalie and keep the ending.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA2UTA3Final: ANA 2, UTA 3

Utah won a hockey game with 12 shots on goal, the first NHL team to win with that few since the Rangers in March 2025, and one of the 12 went into an empty net. Call it efficiency. Leo Carlsson opened the scoring for Anaheim, Vincent Trocheck tied it unassisted, and Andrew Peeke put the Mammoth ahead in the second from Logan Cooley and Daniil But. Cooley's empty-netter with 1:17 left, his 12th, ended up as the winner when Ian Moore scored with 12 seconds to go. In between, Sebastian Cossa stopped 29 of 31 while his teammates took the night off in front of him, and Utah did it without Clayton Keller, a late scratch with an illness. The Mammoth are 12-9-3. The Ducks outshot a team 31-12 and lost, which takes a level of commitment to disappointment that Anaheim has been perfecting for years.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN3VAN4SOFinal: MIN 3, VAN 4 SO

Marco Rossi hadn't scored in 21 games, so naturally he scored twice against Minnesota, the second with the goalie pulled and 1:23 left, 35 seconds after Nick Foligno looked like he'd won it for the Wild. Luke Schenn and Marcus Foligno fought two minutes in to set the mood. Matt Boldy (his 14th) and Jared Spurgeon scored for Minnesota, both set up by Kirill Kaprizov, whose 14-game point streak ties the franchise record; the Wild have points in 14 straight themselves. Rossi on the power play and Zeev Buium, with his first of the season, kept Vancouver level, and Brock Boeser assisted on three goals to push his point streak to a career-high 10 games. Jake DeBrusk had the only goal of the shootout, and Leevi Meriläinen, 22 saves on 25 shots, stopped Maxim Shabanov, Boldy and Kaprizov. Jesper Wallstedt made 21 saves. Minnesota was 83 seconds from two points and settled for one, plus a reminder from a guy who used to wear the sweater.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SEA3SJS4Final: SEA 3, SJS 4

Kaapo Kakko scored on the power play to put Seattle ahead, and the Kraken enjoyed that lead for all of 29 seconds. Michael Misa tied it, Nolan Allan put San Jose in front, and Macklin Celebrini (his 10th) and Ivar Stenberg added power-play goals to make it 4-1 before the game was half over. Dmitry Orlov assisted on three of the four, and Celebrini and Stenberg, a goal and an assist apiece, look like a problem the Pacific Division will be filing complaints about for a decade. Seattle made it interesting with second-period goals from Matty Beniers and Ryan Winterton, then spent the third finding out Alex Nedeljkovic was done giving: 27 saves on 30 shots. Philipp Grubauer stopped 25 of 29. The Kraken took the penalties, the Sharks took the points, and Seattle remains the league's most reliably forgettable way to spend a Saturday night.

4
FinalLenovo Center
7
Carolina HurricanesCAR17-3-3 · 37 pts36 shots
1st2nd3rdTEDM2204CAR0527

Puckline's Report

Edmonton led 3-1 in Raleigh, which in Oilers terms is the part of the horror movie where somebody says they'll be right back. Owen Michaels, Leon Draisaitl (his 22nd, on the power play) and a shorthanded Mathieu Joseph built the lead, and then Carolina scored six of the next seven. Jalen Chatfield, Taylor Hall and Andrei Svechnikov struck in a 3:05 stretch of the second, Sebastian Aho put the Hurricanes ahead for good on the power play with 26 seconds left in the period, and Svechnikov and Alexander Nikishin finished it. Carolina scored three power-play goals, and Aho had a goal and two assists. Pyotr Kochetkov won while stopping 11 of 15, a save percentage usually reserved for beer league. Devon Levi faced 36 shots and a penalty kill that kills nothing but Edmonton's evenings.

CHI 4–3 CGY OT

Chicago BlackhawksCHI7-14-2 · 16 pts33 shots
4
Final/OTScotiabank Saddledome
3
Calgary FlamesCGY10-12-2 · 22 pts36 shots
1st2nd3rdOTTCHI03014CGY11103

Puckline's Report

Dillon Boucher and Adam Klapka dropped the gloves four seconds in, which turned out to be the most organized thing Calgary did all night. Ryan Strome gave the Flames the lead, then Chicago scored three times in 3:05 of the second: Roman Kantserov's 10th, Ryan Donato with the extra attacker on and Patrick Kane on the power play. Calgary clawed back through Jonathan Castagna and a Yegor Sharangovich power-play goal early in the third, but Sam Rinzel ended it at 4:45 of overtime, his third point of the night. Kane, who apparently plans to do this until the sun burns out, had a goal and two assists. Spencer Knight stopped 33 of 36; Dustin Wolf stopped 29 of 33 and deserved a better cause. The Flames got a point, which is what Calgary calls a moral victory and the standings call 3-on-3 charity.

Florida PanthersFLA13-8-3 · 29 pts30 shots

Puckline's Report

Sam Bennett spent Saturday treating the Sabres like a rental car. He scored three minutes in, answered Jack Quinn's go-ahead goal 18 seconds later, and put Florida in front shorthanded 48 seconds into the third for the hat trick, his eighth, ninth and 10th of the season. Buffalo, to its credit, kept getting up: Jiri Kulich, Quinn and Tage Thompson (his 15th) each tied or led. So Bennett went and set up Sandis Vilmanis for the winner with 3:18 left, a four-point night. Jacob Markstrom needed only 16 saves on 19 shots. Alex Lyon stopped 26 of 30 and is 0-3-1 since coming back, and Lindy Ruff said his team got beat at the net front on the winner. The Sabres are 9-10-4, a record that looks exactly like every Sabres record you have ever seen.

Puckline's Report

The Penguins led 2-0 in Nashville, and Andrei Kuzmenko, a healthy scratch in five of the previous six games, scored his first goal in black and gold. That was the good part, and it lasted about 70 seconds. Jonathan Marchessault got one back before the first period ended, Filip Forsberg and Reid Schaefer scored in the first 6:22 of the second, and after Hendrix Lapierre tied it at 3, Jayden Struble won it 3:31 into the third off feeds from Steven Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly. Marchessault and Brady Skjei had two points each, Juuse Saros stopped 21 of 24, and Sergei Murashov made 25 saves in the loss. Samuel Girard had the other Pittsburgh goal with Tommy Novak in the top-line seat beside Sidney Crosby. Ottawa's general manager watched from the press box, and the Penguins played like a team that knew the store was open.

Puckline's Report

Elias Lindholm scored four goals, and at no point did anyone in a Capitals sweater seem interested in finding out where he was standing. He scored on the power play in the first, twice in the second and again 4:07 into the third, and set up David Pastrnak in between for a five-point night. Morgan Geekie had three assists, Tanner Jeannot scored, and even Jeremy Swayman picked up an assist while stopping 30 of 35. Washington kept it a game: Tom Wilson, a shorthanded Alex Tuch, Pierre-Luc Dubois and Dylan Strome had it tied 4-4 in the second, and Jakob Chychrun made it 6-5 late before Fraser Minten hit the empty net. Charlie Lindgren allowed six on 22 shots. That's five straight losses and a sub-.500 record for the Capitals, and Spencer Carbery said that if you cannot defend in this league, you will never win. Seven goals against is a strong supporting argument.

Puckline's Report

The Maple Leafs led 3-1 at home and lost, because of course they did, and because the hockey gods have a sense of humor the winning rally ran through Matthew Knies, the winger Toronto traded to Columbus in September. Auston Matthews (his 14th, on the power play), Jake McCabe and Teddy Blueger built the lead. Knies set up Adam Fantilli's power-play goal in the second, tied it himself, unassisted, with 4:20 left, and 52 seconds later Zach Werenski scored the winner from Fantilli. Cam Talbot made 23 saves; Anthony Stolarz stopped 31 of 35 and has seen this movie. That's nine straight losses, 0-8-1, for an 8-14-3 team whose coach, Jim Hiller, called the night just not National Hockey League level. Toronto has spent decades finding new ways to lose. Getting beat by its own trade is at least efficient.

Puckline's Report

Montreal spent the third period erasing a two-goal deficit and the last 31 seconds finding out none of it mattered. Noah Cates scored at 19:29, from Sean Couturier and Matvei Michkov, and the Flyers walked out of the Bell Centre with both points and most of the building's good mood. Christian Dvorak opened the scoring, Oliver Kapanen answered 16 seconds later, and Denver Barkey (a goal and an assist) and Rasmus Ristolainen made it 3-1 in the second, both set up by Owen Tippett. Zachary Bolduc on the power play and Owen Beck tied it 74 seconds apart early in the third. Dan Vladar stopped 20 of 23. Jacob Fowler saw 20 shots and four of them went in, which is a rough way to spend a Saturday night in front of 21,000 amateur goalie coaches. The Canadiens did the hard part and then forgot the easy part: the last half-minute.

Puckline's Report

For most of two periods the Kings led 1-0 on a Mats Zuccarello goal and played the kind of hockey that makes you check your phone. Then Nick Cousins tied it with 54 seconds left in the second, and Tim Stützle decided the third period was his. He scored 30 seconds in, set up Stephen Halliday's power-play goal at 5:54 and scored again at 7:16: three Ottawa goals in 6:46, three points for Stützle, his 12th and 13th of the season. Dylan Cozens and Jake Sanderson had two assists each. Linus Ullmark stopped 19 of 21 and was mostly asked to stay awake. Anton Forsberg made 24 saves, and Quinton Byfield's late goal made the score look friendlier than the period was. Los Angeles held a lead for two periods and had no idea what to do with it, the same way it handles the first round.

Puckline's Report

Ondrej Palat came into the night with two goals all season and left Detroit with four, which tells you what kind of evening the Red Wings had. Emmitt Finnie put Detroit up in the first, Palat tied it in the second, Simon Holmstrom scored his 10th early in the third to stretch his point streak to seven games, and Palat's second made it 3-1. Alex DeBrincat answered 29 seconds later, and that was all. Matthew Schaefer had two assists and now has 85 career points, passing Rasmus Dahlin for the second most by a teenage defenseman; only Phil Housley had more. Ilya Sorokin stopped 18 of 20, John Gibson 18 of 21, and Ben Chiarot and Brayden Schenn fought late in the second for the purists. The Islanders have points in seven straight. Detroit managed 20 shots at home, a rebuild now old enough to ask for the car keys.

Puckline's Report

Fifteen goals in St. Louis, and somewhere a goalie coach is updating his resume. The Blues led 3-0 before six minutes were gone on goals from Brandon Carlo, Jimmy Snuggerud (his 13th, on the power play) and Robert Thomas, and when Philip Broberg made it 4-1 at 9:03, Connor Hellebuyck's night was over: four goals on six shots. Jake Allen came in and gave up four more. Jake Neighbours had five assists, the kind of line you normally need a video game to produce, and Broberg, Thomas and Logan Mailloux each had a goal and two assists. New Jersey never went away, getting within one twice on goals from Timo Meier, Luke Hughes and Connor Brown, but Pavel Buchnevich, Mailloux, Mason McTavish and Jonatan Berggren (twice, one into the empty net) kept answering. Jordan Binnington allowed six on 43 shots and won comfortably. The Devils scored six and lost by three, which is less a hockey game than a cry for help.

Puckline's Report

Adam Lowry scored 29 seconds in and the Jets still found a way to hand out a souvenir point and keep none of the good ones. Vegas answered through Brett Howden and Mitch Marner, Viggo Björck tied it before the first intermission, and the teams traded from there: Tomas Hertl's 10th on the power play, Mark Scheifele, then Kyle Connor's 19th to put Winnipeg up 4-3 early in the third. Ivan Barbashev tied it with 3:35 left, and in the shootout William Karlsson scored the only goal while Carter Hart turned away Scheifele, Connor and Gabriel Vilardi. Jack Eichel had two assists, Hertl and Howden a goal and an assist each. Hart stopped 26 of 30; Stuart Skinner made 29 saves and lost anyway. Winnipeg led twice at home and went 0-for-3 in the skills contest, proof that you can change the goalie and keep the ending.

Puckline's Report

Utah won a hockey game with 12 shots on goal, the first NHL team to win with that few since the Rangers in March 2025, and one of the 12 went into an empty net. Call it efficiency. Leo Carlsson opened the scoring for Anaheim, Vincent Trocheck tied it unassisted, and Andrew Peeke put the Mammoth ahead in the second from Logan Cooley and Daniil But. Cooley's empty-netter with 1:17 left, his 12th, ended up as the winner when Ian Moore scored with 12 seconds to go. In between, Sebastian Cossa stopped 29 of 31 while his teammates took the night off in front of him, and Utah did it without Clayton Keller, a late scratch with an illness. The Mammoth are 12-9-3. The Ducks outshot a team 31-12 and lost, which takes a level of commitment to disappointment that Anaheim has been perfecting for years.

Puckline's Report

Marco Rossi hadn't scored in 21 games, so naturally he scored twice against Minnesota, the second with the goalie pulled and 1:23 left, 35 seconds after Nick Foligno looked like he'd won it for the Wild. Luke Schenn and Marcus Foligno fought two minutes in to set the mood. Matt Boldy (his 14th) and Jared Spurgeon scored for Minnesota, both set up by Kirill Kaprizov, whose 14-game point streak ties the franchise record; the Wild have points in 14 straight themselves. Rossi on the power play and Zeev Buium, with his first of the season, kept Vancouver level, and Brock Boeser assisted on three goals to push his point streak to a career-high 10 games. Jake DeBrusk had the only goal of the shootout, and Leevi Meriläinen, 22 saves on 25 shots, stopped Maxim Shabanov, Boldy and Kaprizov. Jesper Wallstedt made 21 saves. Minnesota was 83 seconds from two points and settled for one, plus a reminder from a guy who used to wear the sweater.

Puckline's Report

Kaapo Kakko scored on the power play to put Seattle ahead, and the Kraken enjoyed that lead for all of 29 seconds. Michael Misa tied it, Nolan Allan put San Jose in front, and Macklin Celebrini (his 10th) and Ivar Stenberg added power-play goals to make it 4-1 before the game was half over. Dmitry Orlov assisted on three of the four, and Celebrini and Stenberg, a goal and an assist apiece, look like a problem the Pacific Division will be filing complaints about for a decade. Seattle made it interesting with second-period goals from Matty Beniers and Ryan Winterton, then spent the third finding out Alex Nedeljkovic was done giving: 27 saves on 30 shots. Philipp Grubauer stopped 25 of 29. The Kraken took the penalties, the Sharks took the points, and Seattle remains the league's most reliably forgettable way to spend a Saturday night.

CAR @ NYR · 12:30 PM ET

Carolina HurricanesCAR17-3-3 · 37 PTSML -162
@12:30 PM ETSun Nov 22 · Madison Square Garden
CAR -162MLNYR +134
New York RangersNYR13-8-1 · 27 PTSML +134

Puckline Preview

Carolina rolls into Madison Square Garden for a 12:30 matinee the day after hanging seven on Edmonton, the fourth time this season the Hurricanes have scored seven in a game. They're 17-3-3 with a plus-42 goal differential, Sebastian Aho has 32 points in 23 games and Andrei Svechnikov is up to 13 goals. The catch: it's the second half of a back-to-back, Nikolaj Ehlers didn't make the trip after getting hurt Saturday (not his knee, Rod Brind'Amour says), and Sean Walker gets to celebrate his 500th NHL game on short sleep.

Brandon Bussi starts in the Carolina net, the Hurricanes say, and the Rangers remember him. The Long Island kid who grew up a Rangers fan shut them out 2-0 in this building in February, a night New York managed 10 shots through two periods, one day after trading Artemi Panarin. Things are sunnier now: the Rangers have won three straight, allowed one goal in each and have had five days off. They're doing it without Igor Shesterkin, who is done for the season, so it's Dylan Garand or Joonas Korpisalo (nobody had named a starter as of late morning), with Max Sasson, picked up from Vancouver on Friday, projected to debut on the fourth line. One team is rested, the other is a wagon with tired legs. Somebody's excuse is already written.

By Puckline Prince

BUF @ TBL · 5:00 PM ET

Buffalo SabresBUF9-10-4 · 22 PTSML +172
@5:00 PM ETSun Nov 22 · Benchmark International Arena
BUF +172MLTBL -210
Tampa Bay LightningTBL15-5-2 · 32 PTSML -210

Puckline Preview

Eleven days ago the Lightning walked into Buffalo and won 8-3. The Sabres had it at 4-3 early in the third, and then Nikita Kucherov scored a natural hat trick, John Carlson finished with five points and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen got the hook after five goals on 14 shots. Tonight Buffalo gets the rematch in Tampa, on the second night of a back-to-back, in the last game of a six-game road trip. The schedule-maker has jokes.

The Sabres are 9-10-4 and 1-5-1 since Nov. 8, and they lost 4-3 in Florida on Saturday on a goal with 3:18 left. Nobody has named a starter: Alex Lyon, 0-3-1 since coming back from injury, played Saturday, so it's Luukkonen, who didn't even dress as the backup in Florida with no reason given, or Colten Ellis. There are bright spots, as there always are in Buffalo right before they go out: Tage Thompson has 15 goals and Jiri Kulich looked like himself on the top line. Tampa Bay is 15-5-2 and 10-1-0 at home, and on Thursday it held Connor McDavid off the scoresheet to end his season-opening 23-game point streak. The Lightning are without Conor Geekie, Brandon Hagel is unlikely to play and Zemgus Girgensons is questionable. Buffalo did go 3-0-1 against these guys last season. Buffalo also remembers what last season got them.

By Puckline Prince

EDM @ STL · 7:00 PM ET

Edmonton OilersEDM17-5-3 · 37 PTSML +105
@7:00 PM ETSun Nov 22 · Enterprise Center
EDM +105MLSTL -126
St Louis BluesSTL12-9-2 · 26 PTSML -126

Puckline Preview

These two played separate games on Saturday that produced 26 goals between them, so if you came for defense, the exits are clearly marked. St. Louis beat New Jersey 9-6 for its third straight win and has 22 goals in its last three games. Jake Neighbours tied the club record with five assists and has nine points in three games, Robert Thomas has three straight three-point nights and Jimmy Snuggerud is up to 13 goals. Jim Montgomery still called it sloppy, which is a bold thing to say about a team allowing six a night and winning anyway.

Edmonton led Carolina 3-1 and lost 7-4, its second straight regulation loss, something that hadn't happened to the 17-5-3 Oilers all season. The penalty kill has given up four goals on its last eight chances, Connor McDavid (57 points in 25 games, which is not a typo) had two assists and zero shots, and this is the last stop of a six-game road trip. Zach Hyman left Saturday with a migraine and is questionable; Ryan Nugent-Hopkins has been cleared, but the plan is to hold him out until Tuesday. Connor McMichael is questionable for the Blues. In goal, Tristan Jarry starts for Edmonton after Devon Levi faced 36 shots, and Joel Hofer goes for St. Louis after Jordan Binnington played Saturday. It's the first meeting of the season. The Blues won the last one 3-2 in overtime in March.

By Puckline Prince

@7:00 PM ETSun Nov 22 · American Airlines Center
PIT +190MLDAL -235
Dallas StarsDAL14-6-2 · 30 PTSML -235

Puckline Preview

The Penguins have led after the first period in each of their last three games and lost all three, a bit they keep committing to. Saturday it was a 2-0 lead in Nashville that became a 4-3 loss, and now Pittsburgh (7-13-2, 2-7-1 in its last 10) lands in Dallas on the second night of a back-to-back without Evgeni Malkin, who didn't make the trip. Arturs Silovs is the expected starter, though nobody has said so. Dan Muse says his team is pressing. Ottawa's general manager was in the press box Saturday amid reports the Senators like Rickard Rakell and Bryan Rust, so at least somebody is enjoying Penguins games.

Dallas is 14-6-2 and has won four straight, three of them past regulation, including two late comebacks in Vegas. The Stars' own website called their first quarter a beautiful mess, and it fits: they sit 25th in the league in shots and keep winning anyway. Wyatt Johnston has goals in four straight games. The one meeting this season went to Pittsburgh, 2-1 in a shootout on Oct. 10, after Tyler Seguin tied it with 30 seconds left. Extra spice: Elliotte Friedman has reported these two teams got far down the road on a Jason Robertson trade at the draft. Robertson stayed, and he has 13 points in 10 career games against Pittsburgh. Sidney Crosby, for his part, has 27 points in 27 games against Dallas. Somebody still shows up to work.

By Puckline Prince

CHI @ VAN · 8:00 PM ET

Chicago BlackhawksCHI7-14-2 · 16 PTSML -114
@8:00 PM ETSun Nov 22 · Rogers Arena
CHI -114MLVAN -105
Vancouver CanucksVAN6-18-1 · 13 PTSML -105

Puckline Preview

Somebody has to win this one, and the standings would like a word about that. Chicago is 7-14-2, Vancouver is 6-18-1, and the Canucks and Blackhawks rank 32nd and 31st in goals allowed at 4.32 and 4.00 a game. Both played Saturday, both won past regulation, and both are expected to hand the net to someone new: Drew Commesso could make his season debut for Chicago, and Nikita Tolopilo, just up from Abbotsford, could go for Vancouver. Neither team has named a starter. Tolopilo was in net the last time these two met, a 6-3 Canucks win in Chicago in March.

The Blackhawks got their first road win of the season in Calgary on Sam Rinzel's overtime goal, with Patrick Kane ending an 18-game goal drought and rookie Roman Kantserov scoring his 10th. The bad news is heavier: Connor Bedard is headed for shoulder surgery and likely out three to four months, Anton Frondell left Saturday's game and is uncertain, and Wyatt Kaiser has a Player Safety hearing for his hit on Martin Pospisil. Vancouver is without Elias Pettersson, but Brock Boeser has a career-high 10-game point streak and Marco Rossi just scored twice after 21 games of nothing. Also: the Canucks' penalty kill is running at 63 percent. Chicago's power play is 27th. Something has to give, or possibly nothing will.

By Puckline Prince
